overall: The AG ordered the committee to release five sets of executive session minutes and four categories of documents used at meetings, finding the discipline-related executive session purpose had concluded; scope of the broader records request was limited to documents used by the body.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee withheld executive session minutes from its discipline-related meetings after the purpose for those sessions had ended.
allegations.key_passage: In our opinion, these declaratory statements of the Committee make clear its intent that the purpose for entering executive session to discuss the discipline of an employee on May 28th, June 29th, July 19th, August 30th and September 8th was now concluded.

allegations.summary: Complainant sought release of documents used at the committee's meetings on the superintendent matter, which the committee had not released.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, consistent with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law, we order that the following documents "used at the meeting[s]" of the Committee be made available to the public, subject to G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f):

allegations.summary: Executive session minutes from several meetings did not include the list of documents used at the meeting, as the revised Open Meeting Law requires.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Committee minutes from the executive sessions convened on July 12th, July 19th, August 30th and September 8th do not include a list of documents and other exhibits used at the meeting as required by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee stated the purpose of several executive sessions as discipline of an employee; the AG reviewed whether that purpose was valid.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, in each of these instances, this was an appropriately stated purpose under the law.

allegations.summary: The AG itself flagged that the May 28 executive session was convened by roll call without stating any lawful purpose before discussion began.
allegations.key_passage: However, at no time prior to taking the roll call vote to enter executive session and beginning discussions in earnest did the Committee cite one of the purposes allowed under the law.

allegations.summary: Complainant requested all records of counsel, school counsel, and the superintendent and his counsel relating to the matter; the AG addressed how far the request reaches.
allegations.key_passage: Documents not used by the public body, and documents used by individuals other than members of the public body which are not in the custody of the public body, are necessarily excluded from those documents "used" by the public body and are not part of the official record.

remedy: Release the executive session minutes of May 28, June 29, July 19, August 30, and September 8, 2010, subject to the Public Records Law, within ten days of receipt of the determination.

Release the documents used at the May 10, May 28-June 29, July 19, August 30, and September 8, 2010 meetings: the superintendent-related writing, the impoundment letter, the amended main motion, and the draft public statements.
remedy_passage: The Committee shall make the minutes available in a timely manner and no later than ten (10) days from the receipt of this determination.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
